reason: Intentional cross-board feedback ingress, not a board-content API. POST authenticates getSessionUser(request.headers), validates text/kind/notify/context, then reads only the fixed FEEDBACK_PROJECT_ID=15 and fixed destination section. The query supplies destination metadata and owner for createProvisionedTaskCore and notifications; POST returns only {success:true}, never the project or its contents. Requiring submitters to be members of board 15 would break customer feedback. Existing feedback-route-board-15 tests and HTPR-7508 boundary tests cover authenticated submission without membership and signed-out refusal.

reason: validateMcpAuth supplies ctx.user, ctx.agentId and ctx.teamScope. The initial project lookup only resolves the requested ID; no field is returned before the immediately following access gate. Team-scoped or enforced-agent callers must pass prisma.project.findFirst with the same projectId and projectContentAccessWhere(ctx.user.id, ctx.agentId, ctx.teamScope). Other callers must be the owner or a human member. Notifications retain the scoped task.project predicate. tests/htpr-7179-inbox-analytics-scope.test.cjs exercises WATCH, ENFORCE and flag errors with bound/unbound/human callers, allowed board A notifications and forbidden board B changes.

Intentional global aggregate admin endpoint. Before getProjectCounts/getTaskCounts and every Prisma/raw count, the handler requires both a verified getSessionUser identity and a configured ADMIN_USER_RESET_PW matching x-admin-password. A normal human or agent session alone is insufficient. Counts expose global totals only to this explicit administrator capability, so filtering by board membership would corrupt the admin report. tests/htpr-7508-reviewed-boundaries.test.cjs covers signed-out, missing/wrong/unconfigured password refusal without database access and still-allowed session-plus-password aggregate responses.
